answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil attacks by making reputation tidal: trust weight flows like a tide — slow to rise, quick to drain — so a lone identity that behaves well gradually gains standing, while a sudden wave of correlated newcomers has its influence bled away on detection. A rare, high-effort "comet" milestone — a costly, publicly verified contribution — becomes the only fast path to real weight. Identities accrete like a coral reef: many small, checkable contributions stacked over time. Fakes can arrive in swarms, but they cannot fast-track the slow accumulation of trust.
